key_claims: Excitatory and inhibitory synaptic density remain at steady-state levels during synapse maturation despite continual synaptic turnover.
The study developed imaging and analysis methods to visualize and track excitatory and inhibitory synapses simultaneously.
Subsets of synapses are forming and eliminating even in mature hippocampal neurons, yet excitatory and inhibitory synapse levels remain balanced over time.
limitations: The study was performed in primary hippocampal neuron cultures and ex vivo hippocampal slices, which may not fully replicate in vivo conditions.
The imaging period was limited to 15 hours, which may not capture longer-term synaptic dynamics.
The analysis focused on 'still' neurites, potentially excluding dynamic neurites from the quantitative tracking.
The study used fluorescently tagged synaptic proteins, which might alter endogenous protein behavior.
what_not_to_say: The study proves that excitatory-inhibitory balance is maintained in all neural circuits.
The study identifies a specific molecular mechanism for synaptic balance.
The study provides clinical recommendations for neurodevelopmental disorders.
The study shows that synaptic turnover rates are the same across all brain regions or cell types.

key_claims: Disrupted body clock is linked to higher dementia risk.
The article reports on a study that found an association between disrupted circadian rhythms and increased risk of dementia.
The article suggests that maintaining a regular body clock may be important for brain health.
limitations: The article does not provide details on the study design or sample size.
The article does not specify the exact measure of body clock disruption.
The article does not mention potential confounding factors.
The article does not provide effect sizes or statistical significance.
what_not_to_say: The article does not claim that disrupted body clock causes dementia.
The article does not provide specific numbers or statistics.
The article does not mention any specific interventions to improve body clock.

key_claims: The study provides the first open-access CBCT IQA dataset containing 1,764 annotated image slices.
The dataset was acquired using systematic variations in image acquisition and reconstruction parameters.
Three clinical experts graded overall image quality and predefined regions of interest using a four-level scoring scheme.
The study benchmarks 26 full-reference and no-reference IQA measures against expert annotations.
An exploratory IQA measure-based ranking was introduced to distinguish subtle image quality differences.
limitations: The source does not specify the exact acquisition and reconstruction parameters used.
The source does not provide details on the four-level scoring scheme.
The source does not specify which IQA measures were benchmarked.
The source does not report quantitative results of the benchmarking.
what_not_to_say: The dataset is clinically validated for diagnostic use.
The IQA measures outperform expert evaluation.
The dataset includes patient outcomes or diagnostic accuracy data.
The study establishes a causal relationship between image quality and diagnostic accuracy.
